overview: Liverpool retained the European Cup, beating Club Brugge 1–0 at Wembley on 10 May. Kenny Dalglish scored the winner after a pass from Graeme Souness, completing a first Liverpool season in which he led the scoring with 31 goals in all competitions.

Dalglish had arrived from Celtic after Kevin Keegan’s departure for Hamburg, while Souness joined from Middlesbrough in January. Liverpool also won the European Super Cup, beating Hamburg 7–1 on aggregate. Terry McDermott scored a hat-trick in the 6–0 second-leg win at Anfield.

At home, Liverpool finished runners-up in the First Division, seven points behind Nottingham Forest. Forest also beat them 1–0 in the League Cup final replay after a goalless first match. Chelsea ended Liverpool’s FA Cup run in the third round, while the Charity Shield was shared with Manchester United.

events.title: The first European Super Cup
events.detail: Liverpool beat Hamburg 6–0 at Anfield to complete a 7–1 aggregate victory.

events.title: The European Cup retained
events.detail: Dalglish scored the only goal against Club Brugge at Wembley.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: European Cup
sources.claims: First win on 25 May 1977, 3–1 against Borussia Mönchengladbach with McDermott, Smith and Neal scoring; retained on 10 May 1978 through Dalglish against Club Brugge.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Charity and Community Shield
sources.claims: Outright winners in 1974 and 1976; shared with Manchester United in 1977. The club attributes the 1974 match to Paisley.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Kenny Dalglish
sources.claims: Joined from Celtic in August 1977 for £440,000 after Keegan left for Hamburg; led scoring with 31 goals in his first season including the 1978 European Cup winner; Football Writers’ Footballer of the Year in 1979.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: UEFA Super Cup
sources.claims: First won on 6 December 1977, following 1–1 away and 6–0 home results against Hamburg; McDermott hat-trick. Anderlecht won the following edition 4–3 on aggregate.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Graeme Souness
sources.claims: Joined from Middlesbrough and supplied the pass for Dalglish’s goal in the 1978 European Cup final.
